kjv: O Lucifer, son of the morning
mine: O Shining One, son of Dawn
note: Hebrew helel ben-shachar "shining one, son of dawn" (the morning star, Venus) is a taunt against the king of Babylon (v. 4). "Lucifer" is the Vulgate's Latin for the morning star; the KJV kept it as a proper name, which fostered its later identification with Satan. Context: Shining One, son of Dawn, said of the king of Babylon (high confidence). 14:4 introduces the taunt 'against the king of Babylon'; 14:16 'is this the man who made the earth tremble?'
Hebrew qippod is probably the hedgehog or porcupine (cf. Arabic qunfudh), though some take it as a bird.
Hebrew tsepha' is a venomous snake (viper); the "cockatrice" was a mythical serpent hatched from a cock's egg.
